The regression faithfully injects termination failure at the OS boundary while retaining real process spawning: POSIX denies the owned process-group SIGKILL; Windows replaces execFile before export synchronization and fresh module import, avoiding the real executable's custom promisifier.

Assertions remain intact for E_CHECK_FAILED, the original 2000ms timeout, the injected cleanup-denial reason, both stdout/stderr tails, rejection before 5000ms, and real shell and foreground-child existence before independent cleanup. The watchdog cannot satisfy the expected rejection assertions.

POSIX independent cleanup now kills the captured foreground child, falling back to the owned fixture's check.pid. It leaves the shell available to reap that child, awaits close with a 3000ms watchdog, and retains final ESRCH assertions for both recorded PIDs on the successful assertion path. Windows cleanup is unchanged. The close watchdog does not establish a total finally duration below 3000ms.

Failure-path fixture limitations remain: an early failure before PID-file availability can make fallback reading fail; final foreground-child ESRCH is conditional on foregroundPid having been assigned. These do not establish a new normal-path defect or invalidate the preserved two-PID assertions when the regression reaches its intended path.

The carried release-gate-repairs-r1-20261003/report.json is immutable historical provenance for the earlier 550f review and Windows execution, not current POSIX runtime proof. Its fixed disposition does not independently establish acceptance of this repair.
